claims.statement: Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified an evolving fake-download campaign in which users executed deceptive installers presented as cracked software, games, activators, plugins or unofficial utilities, and the installers distributed multiple monetized software offers.
The source-observed chain used Inno Setup-style temporary runners under %TEMP%\is-*.tmp and recurring numbered stages before downstream offer delivery.

The delivery system used randomized URL paths but preserved d=inno together with r=offer_execution or r=offer_execution_fail; callbacks represented individual offer results and failed offers did not necessarily stop the full bundle.

Microsoft observed rotating callback domains across recurring lure categories and assessed the paired callback structure, together with adjacent installer activity, as more durable than individual domains.

The investigation confirmed proxy and network-resource monetization through WorldProxyPool, distributed-compute monetization through CharityEngine and BOINC, and utility-style software installation; the WorldProxyPool branch created recurring SYSTEM scheduled tasks.
Microsoft published a Defender XDR advanced-hunting query that filters DeviceNetworkEvents RemoteUrl for d=inno and either r=offer_execution or r=offer_execution_fail.

Microsoft documents DeviceNetworkEvents as Defender for Endpoint network-connection telemetry and documents RemoteUrl, remote endpoint, initiating-process and compound event-identity fields used or projected by the query.

A query result proves only that Defender XDR recorded a RemoteUrl matching both callback conditions; it does not establish fake-installer execution, offer success, installation, monetization, compromise or attribution.
claims.confirm_or_refute: Preserve the raw network event and correlate process ancestry, download provenance, staged files, protection events, scheduled tasks and software inventory. Without those independent artifacts, retain the callback-only boundary.

claims.statement: The paired callback structure is suitable for hunting, but RemoteUrl capture semantics, required-field completeness and legitimate bundler prevalence must be measured before alert promotion.
claims.confirm_or_refute: Run the authorized paired-marker positive and single-marker negative controls, inspect raw RemoteUrl values and resolve historical matches. Consistent capture plus bounded overlap supports promotion; absent query strings or unbounded legitimate matches refute it.

claims.statement: MITRE ATT&CK T1071.001 is the defensible mapping for the source-observed HTTP callback behavior queried by this package.
The Microsoft report was published on 3 November 2026 and describes an evolving campaign without exact public start and end dates.
Microsoft notes that several downstream products may have legitimate uses, while their silent installation through deceptive bundles without informed consent creates security and privacy risk.
Microsoft observed child payloads launching before or around offer callbacks in some EDR traces, so callback time and result markers cannot be treated as a complete prevention or execution verdict.
